title: Vanishing Cech cohomology on a cofinal system of coverings gives vanishing cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $\mathcal B\subset\Ob(X_{\Et})$ be a set of objects and $\mathrm{Cov}$ a set of coverings of $X_{\Et}$, and let $\mathcal F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ be an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For an object $U$ let $H^p(U,-)$ be the $p$-th right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab$, $G\mapsto G(U)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Assume: (1) for every $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$, the objects $U$, $U_i$ and all $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$ lie in $\mathcal B$; (2) for every $U\in\mathcal B$ the coverings of $U$ occurring in $\mathrm{Cov}$ form a cofinal system of coverings of $U$ (every covering of $U$ in $X_{\Et}$ is refined by one in $\mathrm{Cov}$, i.e. each member of the latter factors over $U$ through some member of the former); (3) for every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] satisfies $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$. Then $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $U\in\mathcal B$. (Stacks states this for any site; no finiteness of coverings is assumed. With $\mathcal B=\Ob(X_{\Et})$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ all coverings, (1) and (2) hold automatically.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection) and its proof (embedding into an injective abelian sheaf, Lemma Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), dimension shifting); variant of Cohomology, Lemma 01EV (cohomology-lemma-cech-vanish)

proof.text: **Step 1 (the induction).** Fix $\mathcal B$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ satisfying (1) and (2). Call an abelian sheaf $\mathcal G\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ *Cech-acyclic on* $\mathrm{Cov}$ if $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, i.e. if $\mathcal G$ satisfies (3). For $p\geq1$ let $P(p)$ be the assertion: for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$ Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, $H^p(U,\mathcal G)=0$. We prove $P(p)$ for all $p\geq1$ by induction on $p$, the assertion being quantified over all such $\mathcal G$ at once (Steps 2-6 for a fixed $\mathcal G$, Step 7 the induction); the lemma is $P(p)$ for $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$, which is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ by (3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("Since F was an arbitrary abelian sheaf with vanishing higher Cech cohomology ... And so on and so forth")

proof.text: **Step 2 (embedding into an injective).** Let $\mathcal G$ be Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$. Since $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], choose a monomorphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I$ an injective object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal G$ be its cokernel in the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], so that $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof, first paragraph ("Choose an embedding F -> I into an injective abelian sheaf ... Q = I/F")

proof.text: **Step 3 ($\mathcal I$ is Cech-acyclic).** By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-cech-acyclic], $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every covering $\mathcal U$ of $X_{\Et}$, in particular for every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("By Lemma 03AW I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 4 (sections over objects of $\mathcal B$).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$. The sequence $0\to\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)\to0$ is exact. Exactness at $\mathcal G(U)$ and $\mathcal I(U)$: apply the long exact sequence of the right derived functors of the left exact functor $v=\Gamma(U,-):\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab$, $G\mapsto G(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the sequence of Step 2; its beginning $0\to R^0v(\mathcal G)\to R^0v(\mathcal I)\to R^0v(\mathcal Q)$ is exact, and $R^0v\cong v$ naturally [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], so $0\to\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ is exact. Surjectivity of $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$: by (2) the coverings of $U$ belonging to $\mathrm{Cov}$ form a cofinal system of coverings of $U$, and for each of them $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ because $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$; so [lem-weil-pbc-ses-cech-h1-surjective], applied to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ and this cofinal system, gives that $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ is surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("By Lemma 03F8 and our assumption (2) this sequence gives rise to an exact sequence 0 -> F(U) -> I(U) -> Q(U) -> 0 for every U in B")

proof.text: **Step 5 (short exact sequence of Cech complexes).** Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}\in\mathrm{Cov}$. The morphisms $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q$ induce morphisms of Cech complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)$ (functoriality of the Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex]). In degree $p$ this is the product over $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}$ of the sequences $0\to\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal I(V)\to\mathcal Q(V)\to0$ with $V=U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$; by (1) every such $V$ lies in $\mathcal B$, so each factor is short exact by Step 4, and a product of short exact sequences of abelian groups is short exact (kernels and images of a product of homomorphisms are the products of the kernels and images). Hence $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of abelian groups, short exactness of complexes being degreewise [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("Hence for any U in Cov we get a short exact sequence of Cech complexes ... since each term in the Cech complex is made up out of a product of values over elements of B by assumption (1)")

proof.text: **Step 6 ($\mathcal Q$ is Cech-acyclic).** For $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] of the short exact sequence of Step 5 contains, for each $p\geq1$, the exact piece $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^p}\check H^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. The left term is $0$ by Step 3 and the right term is $0$ since $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p+1>0$; so $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)=0$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is again an abelian sheaf Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("In particular we have a long exact sequence of Cech cohomology groups ... This implies that Q is also an abelian sheaf with vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 7 (dimension shifting).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$ and apply the long exact sequence of the derived functors $H^n(U,-)=R^n\Gamma(U,-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$; since $\mathcal I$ is injective, $H^n(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. Case $p=1$: the piece $H^0(U,\mathcal I)\to H^0(U,\mathcal Q)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G)\to H^1(U,\mathcal I)=0$ is exact, and under $H^0(U,-)\cong\Gamma(U,-)$ [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] its first map is $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$, surjective by Step 4; hence $H^1(U,\mathcal G)=0$. This holds for every $\mathcal G$ Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, which is $P(1)$. Case $p\geq2$, assuming $P(p-1)$: the piece $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal I)=0$ is exact, and $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q)=0$ by $P(p-1)$ applied to $\mathcal Q$, which is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ by Step 6; hence $H^p(U,\mathcal G)=0$, which is $P(p)$. By induction $P(p)$ holds for all $p\geq1$; with $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ (Step 1) this is the lemma.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof, last paragraph (long exact cohomology sequence; H^n(U,I)=0 for n>0 by Derived Categories Lemma 015B; H^1(U,F)=0; H^1(U,Q)=0; H^2(U,F)=0, and so on)

mathlib_searches.query: sheaf with vanishing Cech cohomology for all coverings has vanishing sheaf cohomology
Cech criterion: if an abelian sheaf has trivial higher Cech cohomology for every covering then its higher sheaf cohomology vanishes
